newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's car capital to keep Italian name.
newsitem.headline: Russia's car capital to keep Italian name.

text.p: Russia's automobile capital will keep its unwieldy Italian name after fewer than 50 percent of voters turned out at a referendum which suggested Car City as one of a list of alternatives.

Officials in the Volga city of Togliatti said Sunday's referendum was invalid because of the low turnout. The city, named after late Italian Communist Party leader Palmiro Togliatti, makes the famous -- or infamous -- Lada and Zhiguli cars.
Choices on the ballot were Stavropol-on-the-Volga, the city's name before 1964, Avtograd (which means Car City), Zhiguli and Zhigulevsk.
The city is home to the VAZ auto factory, and has had a link with Italy since a plant building models based on Fiat cars opened there in 1970.
